newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ sees higher pressures from housing.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ sees higher pressures from housing.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand said on Thursday its latest forecasts assumed higher inflationary pressures from housing than previously.

"We've built in somewhat higher inflationary pressures in the housing market over the next few quarters than we had previously, and I think that's being driven partly by indications that the housing market is still alive and well, but partly also of course because the mix of monetary conditions has changed for somewhat lower interest rates than we assumed back in December," Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash said.
Chief Economist David Mayes said the forecasts assumed that construction costs in the CPI would rise by a total of about 12 percent over the years to March 1999.
"What we assumed last time was four percent, so that's the change in our assumptions," Mayes said.
